```{r setup, message=FALSE}
dim(se)

dim(se)
# filters: 385669 -> 18985 transcripts

library(DESeq2)
library(tximeta)
colsums <- colSums(assay(se, "counts"))
cpm <- t(t(assay(se, "counts")) / colsums * 1e6)

# dummy lengths... no correction for length

```

How many samples each donor contributes to each condition, before `ctrl` /
`exp` are relabelled WT / KD below.

```{r samples_per_donor}
samples_per_donor <- as.data.frame(colData(se)) |>
  dplyr::count(donor, condition) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(total = ctrl + exp)

# with a total row
dplyr::bind_rows(
  samples_per_donor,
  dplyr::summarise(samples_per_donor, donor = "total",
                   dplyr::across(c(ctrl, exp, total), sum))
)
```

How the object was built, from `metadata(se)`. tximeta records its own
version, the quantifier and the transcriptome. `quantInfo` holds oarfish's
`meta_info.json` settings, which in this run do not include the oarfish
version (unlike salmon's `salmon_version`), so that has to come from the
original run.

```{r provenance}
md <- metadata(se)
tibble::tibble(
  field = c("tximeta version", "quantifier", "transcriptome", "genome",
            "import time"),
  value = c(as.character(md$tximetaInfo$version), md$tximetaInfo$type,
            md$txomeInfo$index, md$txomeInfo$genome,
            format(md$tximetaInfo$importTime))
)
# oarfish settings, identical across the 11 samples
unique(md$quantInfo$prob_model)
unique(md$quantInfo$alignment_source)
```

## DTU testing with satuRn

We compare the experiment condition (`exp`, RBP knockdown) against
control (`ctrl`) using satuRn.

```{r dtu_design}
colData(se)$condition <- dplyr::case_when(
    colData(se)$condition == "ctrl" ~ "WT",
    colData(se)$condition == "exp" ~ "KD"
)
# KD as reference level
colData(se)$condition <- factor(colData(se)$condition, levels = c("KD", "WT"))

# build design from the factor directly (matches satuRn vignette convention)
condition <- colData(se)$condition
donor <- factor(colData(se)$donor)
design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + condition + donor)

L <- limma::makeContrasts(
  WT_vs_KD = conditionWT - conditionKD,
  levels = design
)
L
```

```{r dtu_fit, message=FALSE}
rowData(se)$isoform_id <- rowData(se)$tx_name
# flatten CharacterList gene_id to plain character
rowData(se)$gene_id <- vapply(rowData(se)$gene_id, `[`, character(1), 1)

se <- se[
  duplicated(rowData(se)$gene_id) |
    duplicated(rowData(se)$gene_id, fromLast = TRUE),
]
# 18985 transcripts -> 11874 transcripts after removing single-isoform genes
se <- satuRn::fitDTU(se, formula = ~0 + condition + donor)
```

```{r dtu_test, message=FALSE}
se <- satuRn::testDTU(
  object = se,
  contrasts = L,
  diagplot1 = TRUE,
  diagplot2 = TRUE
)
```

```{r dtu_results}
gene_ids <- rowData(se)$gene_id

# every tested transcript; `sig_res` below is the significant subset, and the
# non-significant rows are the background pool for slSampleNonEventExons()
dtu_res <- rowData(se)[["fitDTUResult_WT_vs_KD"]] |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("tx_name") |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::mutate(gene_id = gene_ids) |>
  dplyr::select(tx_name, gene_id, estimates, pval, regular_FDR) |>
  dplyr::arrange(pval)

sig_res <- dtu_res |> dplyr::filter(regular_FDR < 0.1)

sig_res <- sig_res |> mutate( tx_id = tx_name)
sig_res
```

How many transcripts and genes are left after the FDR < 0.1 cut, split by the
sign of the estimate (> 0 = higher usage in WT, < 0 = higher usage in KD). A
gene counts as up (or down) when at least one of its significant transcripts
is; a gene with both is one where splicelogic has a pair to compare.

```{r sig_res_summary}
sig_genes <- sig_res |>
  dplyr::group_by(gene_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_up = sum(estimates > 0), n_down = sum(estimates < 0),
                   .groups = "drop")

tibble::tribble(
  ~level,        ~set,                                 ~n,
  "transcripts", "tested",                             nrow(dtu_res),
  "transcripts", "FDR < 0.1",                          nrow(sig_res),
  "transcripts", "FDR < 0.1, estimate > 0 (up, WT)",   sum(sig_res$estimates > 0),
  "transcripts", "FDR < 0.1, estimate < 0 (down, KD)", sum(sig_res$estimates < 0),
  "genes",       "tested",                             dplyr::n_distinct(dtu_res$gene_id),
  "genes",       "with >= 1 FDR < 0.1 transcript",     nrow(sig_genes),
  "genes",       "with >= 1 up transcript",            sum(sig_genes$n_up > 0),
  "genes",       "with >= 1 down transcript",          sum(sig_genes$n_down > 0),
  "genes",       "with >= 1 up and >= 1 down",         sum(sig_genes$n_up > 0 & sig_genes$n_down > 0)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n / n[set == "tested"]),
                .by = level)

```

The same genes split into three groups by the direction of their significant
transcripts, with how many transcripts each group holds. Only the "up and
down" genes can give events; the other two are dropped by the filter below.

```{r sig_gene_classes}
gene_classes <- sig_genes |>
  dplyr::mutate(class = dplyr::case_when(
    n_up > 0 & n_down > 0 ~ "up and down",
    n_up > 0              ~ "up only",
    TRUE                  ~ "down only"
  )) |>
  dplyr::group_by(class = factor(class, levels = c("up only", "down only",
                                                   "up and down"))) |>
  dplyr::summarise(genes = dplyr::n(),
                   transcripts = sum(n_up + n_down),
                   up_tx = sum(n_up),
                   down_tx = sum(n_down)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(class = as.character(class))

# with a total row, which matches the FDR < 0.1 counts in the table above
dplyr::bind_rows(
  gene_classes,
  dplyr::summarise(gene_classes, class = "total",
                   dplyr::across(c(genes, transcripts, up_tx, down_tx), sum))
)
```

```{r sig_res_filtered}
# the significant transcripts, filtered to those with a partner in the same gene:
# keep genes with >= 1 up and >= 1 down transcript (from `sig_genes` above).
# Events always pair an up with a down transcript of the same gene, so this
# only drops transcripts that could never be in an event; the events found
# below are identical with or without it.
paired_genes <- sig_genes$gene_id[sig_genes$n_up > 0 & sig_genes$n_down > 0]
sig_res <- sig_res |> dplyr::filter(gene_id %in% paired_genes)

c(transcripts = nrow(sig_res), genes = dplyr::n_distinct(sig_res$gene_id))

# save sig_res for later use
saveRDS(sig_res, here("workflows/data/sig_res.rds"))
```

```{r load_sig_res}
# load the saved DTU results
sig_res <- readRDS(here("workflows/data/sig_res.rds"))
sig_res
```

## Splice event detection with splicelogic

```{r make_exons, eval=FALSE}
# build exon GRangesList and rename from internal TXID to TXNAME
txdb <- AnnotationDbi::loadDb(here("workflows/data/gencode.v48.sqlite"))
exons <- exonsBy(txdb, by = "tx")
txps <- AnnotationDbi::select(txdb, keys(txdb, "TXID"), c("TXNAME", "GENEID"), "TXID") |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::mutate(TXID = as.character(TXID))
# rename exons to match tx_name in se, matching by TXID
all.equal(names(exons), txps$TXID)
names(exons) <- txps$TXNAME[match(names(exons), txps$TXID)]
saveRDS(exons, here("workflows/data/glinos_exons.rds"))
```

```{r input_formatting}
# load from saved sqlite
txdb <- AnnotationDbi::loadDb(here("workflows/data/gencode.v48.sqlite"))
# load exons from saved rds
exons <- readRDS(here("workflows/data/glinos_exons.rds"))
```

```{r preprare_exons}
# prepare exons for splicelogic
sig_exons <-  prepare_exons(
  txdb, sig_res, coef_col = "estimates", verbose = TRUE
)
#save sl_exons for later use
saveRDS(sig_exons, here("workflows/data/sl_exons_glinos_0.1.rds"))
```

```{r find_events}
#find se
se_events <- sig_exons |> preprocess(coef_col = "estimates")|> find_se()

#find all events
events <- sig_exons |> preprocess(coef_col = "estimates")|> find_all_events()
```


```{r collapse_redundant_events}
# define a helper function
my_paste <- \(x) paste(unique(x), collapse = ",")
# rows are collapsed when they share the same exon and the same event type. The
# exon is identified by `exon_key` (gene, chromosome, start, end and strand),
# built as in the vignette's recipe for an exon id, rather than by `exon_id`:
# the annotation gives the same exon more than one id when it is coding in one
# transcript and non-coding in another
collapsed_events <- events |>
    dplyr::mutate(exon_key = paste(gene_id, seqnames, start, end, strand, sep = ":")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(exon_key, event_type) |>
    plyranges::reduce_ranges_directed(
        n = plyranges::n(),
        exon_id = my_paste(exon_id),
        tx_id = my_paste(tx_id),
        exon_rank = my_paste(exon_rank),
        event_tx_id = my_paste(event_tx_id),
  )
```

```{r barplot_event_types}
event_counts <- events |>
    as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::group_by(event_type) |>
    dplyr::summarise(count = dplyr::n())

collapsed_event_counts <- collapsed_events |>
    as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::group_by(event_type) |>
    dplyr::summarise(count = dplyr::n())

# combine both count tables into one, labelled by source
counts <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  "All events" = event_counts,
  "Collapsed events" = collapsed_event_counts,
  .id = "set"
)

# event types from most to fewest events
counts$event_type <- factor(
  counts$event_type,
  levels = event_counts$event_type[order(-event_counts$count)]
)

ggplot(counts, aes(x = event_type, y = count, fill = set)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "All events" = "#B0CFFF",       # light blue
    "Collapsed events" = "#3A86FF"  # darker blue
  )) +
  labs(title = "Splice event counts",
  x = "Event Type", y = "Count", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r plot_events_by_gene}
# use splicelogic's built-in plotting function to visualize events for one gene,
# picked at random among the genes with events (the seed keeps the same pick on
# every run, as long as the event set does not change)
set.seed(14)
gene_of_interest <- sample(unique(events$gene_id), 1)
# filter events for the gene of interest
events_for_gene <- events[events$gene_id == gene_of_interest]

# visualize the events for the gene of interest
splicelogic::plot_transcripts(events_for_gene, sig_exons, rescale_introns = TRUE) +
  ggtitle(paste("Splice events for gene:", gene_of_interest))
```

```{r save_events_plots, eval=FALSE}
# make a plot for each gene with events and save to files
# plot_transcripts_by_gene returns a list of ggplot objects, one for each gene
plots <- plot_transcripts_by_gene(events, sig_exons)
# save each plot to the same pdf file - takes a while: -- 1725 genes 
pdf(here("workflows/figures/splice_events_by_gene.pdf"), width = 8, height = 6)
for (gene in names(plots)) {
    print(plots[[gene]])
}
dev.off()
```

## Collapse redundant events

`find_se()` returns an exon once per transcript pair it is part of: an exon in
two down transcripts and skipped by two up ones comes back four times. The event counts above already collapse these (`collapsed_events`). For
the sequence analyses below we also keep one row per exon, so that an exon
shared by many transcripts does not weigh more in the profiles and logos, and
the background set is sized by exons rather than pairs. `n` records how many
pairs each exon came from. The collapse is the same as in
`collapse_redundant_events`, applied to the SE events, and like it
collapses rows only for the same exon (gene, chromosome, start, end, strand)
and the same event type.

```{r collapse_se}
# TRUE: the sequence analyses below use one row per exon. FALSE: they use every
# SE event, one row per transcript pair, as before the collapse, to compare
collapse_se <- TRUE

se_collapsed <- se_events |>
    dplyr::mutate(exon_key = paste(gene_id, seqnames, start, end, strand, sep = ":")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(exon_key, event_type) |>
    plyranges::reduce_ranges_directed(
        n = plyranges::n(),
        gene_id = my_paste(gene_id),
        exon_id = my_paste(exon_id),
        tx_id = my_paste(tx_id),
        exon_rank = my_paste(exon_rank),
        event_tx_id = my_paste(event_tx_id),
  )

data.frame(
  set    = c("SE"),
  events = c(length(se_events)),
  exons  = c(length(se_collapsed)),
  max_n  = c(max(se_collapsed$n))
)

# the set the sequence analyses below use
se_exons <- if (collapse_se) se_collapsed else se_events
```

### SE exons per gene

How the SE events spread across genes: the number of distinct SE exons in each
gene. `se_collapsed` already has one row per exon and gene, with `n` the events it
came from, so the counts come straight from it.

```{r se_exons_per_gene, fig.width=6, fig.height=3.5}
se_per_gene <- se_collapsed |>
  dplyr::group_by(gene_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_events = sum(n),
                   n_exons  = plyranges::n())

data.frame(
  se_events = length(se_events),
  se_exons  = length(se_collapsed),
  se_genes  = nrow(se_per_gene)
)

# ggplot needs a data.frame, so the small per-gene summary is converted here
as.data.frame(se_per_gene) |>
  dplyr::count(n_exons) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(n_exons), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3A86FF", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "Distinct SE exons per gene",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d SE events, %d distinct exons, %d genes",
                          length(se_events), length(se_collapsed),
                          nrow(se_per_gene)),
       x = "Distinct SE exons in the gene", y = "Genes") +
  theme_bw()
```

### GO enrichment of SE genes

Which biological processes are the genes with an SE event enriched for? The
test set is every gene with at least one SE event; the background (universe)
is every gene tested for DTU, since only those could give an event. Testing
against the whole genome instead would mostly pick up which genes are expressed
with several isoforms in this tissue. GO biological process terms,
over-representation test with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, and
`clusterProfiler::simplify()` to merge near-identical terms.

```{r go_se_genes, message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
se_genes  <- unique(sub("\\..*", "", as.character(se_events$gene_id)))
universe  <- unique(sub("\\..*", "", dtu_res$gene_id))
c(se_genes = length(se_genes), universe = length(universe))

go_se <- clusterProfiler::enrichGO(
  gene          = se_genes,
  universe      = universe,
  OrgDb         = org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db,
  keyType       = "ENSEMBL",
  ont           = "BP",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
  qvalueCutoff  = 0.2,
  readable      = TRUE   # gene symbols in the geneID column
)
# merge redundant terms (semantic similarity > 0.7), keeping the most
# significant of each group
go_se <- clusterProfiler::simplify(go_se, cutoff = 0.7, by = "p.adjust",
                                   select_fun = min)

go_se_df <- as.data.frame(go_se)
nrow(go_se_df)
go_se_df |>
  dplyr::select(Description, GeneRatio, BgRatio, p.adjust, geneID) |>
  head(20)

if (nrow(go_se_df) > 0) {
  enrichplot::dotplot(go_se, showCategory = 15) +
    labs(title = "GO biological process: genes with an SE event",
         subtitle = sprintf("%d SE genes vs %d DTU-tested genes",
                            length(intersect(se_genes, universe)), length(universe)))
}
```

## Sequence context around the event exons, focusing on skipped exons (SE)

The analysis below uses a set of sequence-context helpers consolidated in
`helper.R` (nucleotide-composition profiles, background exon sampling,
splice-site logos and RBP motif scanning). The splicelogic package itself only
exports `get_seq()` for sequence work, so these stay as paper-repo helpers (for now).

```{r seq_context_helpers, message=FALSE}
source(here("workflows/helper.R"))
```

`slEventFlankProfiles()` takes a finder's output straight away: it flanks each
exon (strand-aware, so "upstream" is 5' in transcription order), slides
overlapping windows across the flank, and returns the per-window nucleotide
fractions for each side.

```{r flank_windows_events, message=FALSE}
se_profiles <- slEventFlankProfiles(se_exons, genome = "hg38", width = 100)

# rows = exons, cols = window_nucleotide (e.g. w1_A)
dim(se_profiles$upstream)
dim(se_profiles$downstream)
```

### Background set

We want to compare the sequence context of the events with that of a control set.
For the control set (non-event exons), we sample as many exons as there are in
`se_exons` (one per SE exon, or one per SE event with `collapse_se = FALSE`),
drawn at random from the internal exons of transcripts with no evidence of
differential usage (`pval > 0.5`).

```{r non_event_exons}
non_event <- slSampleNonEventExons(
  dtu_res, exons, n = se_exons, pval_min = 0.5, seed = 1
)

```

```{r flank_windows_non_event, message=FALSE}
non_event_profiles <- slEventFlankProfiles(
  non_event, genome = "hg38", width = 100
)
dim(non_event_profiles$upstream)
```

The SE profiles stacked over the non-SE ones, on the same axes:

```{r plot_updownstream_events, fig.width=10.5, fig.height=9}
p_se <- slPlotFlankProfiles(se_profiles, exon_label = "SE")

# one shared nucleotide legend at the top
patchwork::wrap_plots(
  p_se,
  slPlotFlankProfiles(non_event_profiles, exon_label = "non-SE"),
  ncol = 1, guides = "collect"
) & theme(legend.position = "top")

# One text size for every poster figure, in pt at 300 dpi: tick labels, axis
# titles, legends and labels inside the plots all use it. se_composition and
# rna_map are drawn at 3.6 x 3 in and 600 dpi, half the size at twice the
# resolution, so they use poster_pt / 2 to come out the same size in pixels.
poster_pt <- 24
half_pt <- poster_pt / 2
same_text <- theme(text = element_text(size = half_pt),
                   axis.text = element_text(size = half_pt),
                   axis.title = element_text(size = half_pt),
                   legend.text = element_text(size = half_pt))

# the SE profile alone, for the poster, styled to sit side by side with the RNA
# map: the same size (3.6 x 3 in), text size, line width and legend layout.
# No plot or legend title (the poster panel's heading and caption carry them),
# but both axis titles are kept. Legend on the top, in one row.
p_se_poster <- slPlotFlankProfiles(se_profiles, exon_label = "SE",
                                   ylim = c(0, 0.5), hlines = seq(0, 0.4, by = 0.2),
                                   base_size = half_pt, linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = NULL) +
  same_text +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "top",
        legend.direction = "horizontal",
        legend.key.width = grid::unit(0.5, "cm"),
        legend.key.height = grid::unit(7, "pt"),
        legend.box.spacing = grid::unit(2, "pt"),
        legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
        plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2))
dir.create(here("workflows", "figures", "poster"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
# a 3.6 x 3 in frame at 600 dpi
ggsave(here("workflows", "figures", "poster", "se_composition.png"), p_se_poster,
       width = 3.6, height = 3, dpi = 600)
```

The two sets, one panel per nucleotide (mean ± standard error), and below
them the difference between them, SE minus non-SE:

```{r plot_se_vs_non_event, fig.width=10.5, fig.height=10}
se_vs_non_event <- list(SE = se_profiles, "non-SE" = non_event_profiles)

p_overlay <- slPlotFlankProfilesByNt(se_vs_non_event)
p_overlay
slPlotFlankProfilesByNt(se_vs_non_event, difference = TRUE)

# poster version: same width as the RNA map (3.6 in), stacked under
# se_composition
# Large text for the poster and no axis or legend titles (the poster caption
# carries them); the nucleotide as a label to the left of each row rather than
# a title above it, to leave the 4 short rows to the data.
p_overlay_poster <- slPlotFlankProfilesByNt(se_vs_non_event,
                                            base_size = 8, linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ nt, ncol = 1, strip.position = "left", scales = "free_y") +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(),
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold", size = 10),
        panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.15, "lines"),
        legend.key.width = grid::unit(0.8, "cm"),
        legend.box.spacing = grid::unit(2, "pt"),
        legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
        plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2))
# a 3.6 in frame at 600 dpi, text and lines halved as for se_composition
ggsave(here("workflows", "figures", "poster", "se_vs_background.png"), p_overlay_poster,
       width = 3.6, height = 2.325, dpi = 600)
```

An alternative, within-transcript control: for each event, the internal exon of
the same transcript that is shared with the event partner and closest in rank
to the event exon.

```{r matched_non_event_exons, eval=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.5}
matched <- slMatchedNonEventExons(se_events, exons)

slEventFlankProfiles(matched, genome = "hg38", width = 100) |>
  slPlotFlankProfiles(exon_label = "matched exon")
```

## Splice-site sequence logos

The window profiles above average over 10 bp, which smooths the splice site
away. `slFlankLogoMatrices()` keeps every base position separate and returns a
position frequency matrix per side, running `width` bases into the intron and
`exon_bases` into the exon so the boundary is inside the matrix.

Note which site each side carries: the region **upstream** of an exon is the
end of the preceding intron and holds the **3' splice site** (acceptor,
`...ag | EXON`); the region **downstream** is the start of the following intron
and holds the **5' splice site** (donor, `EXON | gu...`).

```{r logo_events_bits, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=13, fig.height=3}
se_logo <- slFlankLogoMatrices(se_exons, genome = "hg38",
                               width = 25, exon_bases = 3)

# letter height = information content, the classic logo scaling: unconstrained
# positions shrink to nothing and the consensus stands out
slPlotFlankLogo(se_logo, method = "bits")
```

The same for the background set, to see whether the event splice sites differ
from those of exons in transcripts with no differential usage.

```{r logo_non_event, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=13, fig.height=3}
non_event_logo <- slFlankLogoMatrices(non_event, genome = "hg38",
                                      width = 25, exon_bases = 3)

slPlotFlankLogo(non_event_logo, method = "bits")
```

```{r logo_difference}
# where the two sets differ most, per position and nucleotide
delta <- se_logo$downstream - non_event_logo$downstream
round(delta[, order(-apply(abs(delta), 2, max))[1:6]], 3)
```

## PTBP1 RNA map

Colours below are taken from the package, so they match `plot_transcripts()`:
the up colour for transcripts with higher usage in WT (estimate > 0), the down
colour for higher usage in KD, and `event_palette()` for event types.

```{r plot_setup}
# the package's own colours, read from plot_transcripts() so they stay in sync
sl_up     <- formals(plot_transcripts)$up_color       # higher usage in WT
sl_down   <- formals(plot_transcripts)$down_color     # higher usage in KD
sl_grey   <- formals(plot_transcripts)$unknown_color  # not significant / other
sl_events <- event_palette()

# keep the standard chromosomes only, so every range is in the BSgenome
standard_chr <- function(gr) {
  gr <- GenomeInfoDb::keepStandardChromosomes(gr, pruning.mode = "coarse")
  GenomeInfoDb::seqlevels(gr) <- GenomeInfoDb::seqlevelsInUse(gr)
  gr
}

# the unfiltered counts: the per-sample usage plots use every transcript of a
# gene, not only those kept for DTU
se_raw   <- readRDS(here("workflows/data/GTEx_v9_ONT_SummarizedExperiment.rds"))
raw_gid  <- sub("\\..*", "", vapply(rowData(se_raw)$gene_id, `[`, character(1), 1))
raw_cond <- ifelse(se_raw$condition == "ctrl", "WT", "KD")
raw_cnt  <- assay(se_raw, "counts")
```

SE exons are on down transcripts (higher usage in KD) and skipped in up
transcripts (higher in WT): with PTBP1 present the exon is skipped, so these
are PTBP1-induced skipping events. From PTBP1's RNA map we expect CU-rich
motifs **upstream** of SE exons (around the 3' splice site), relative to the
background exons.

The motif is YCUY (Y = C or U), counted at every start position with
overlapping matches allowed, in `W` nt of intron on each side of the exon. Each
exon gives a 0/1 vector (1 where a motif starts), smoothed with a centred
rolling mean; the profile is the mean ± s.e. across exons. The plot uses the
same layout as the flank profiles above: one axis running through both
introns, with the exon as a grey bar between them.

```{r rna_map, message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
W <- 200
smooth_nt <- 21
motif_regex <- "(?=[CU]CU[CU])"  # lookahead, so overlapping hits all count

# 0/1 matrix, exons x positions: 1 where a motif starts. get_seq() returns the
# sequence in transcription order (minus strand reverse-complemented), and the
# flanks are strand-aware, so column 1 of "upstream" is -W and column W is -1.
flank_matrix <- function(gr, side) {
  gr <- standard_chr(gr)
  fl <- if (side == "upstream") {
    plyranges::flank_upstream(gr, width = W)
  } else {
    plyranges::flank_downstream(gr, width = W)
  }
  seqs <- as.character(get_seq(fl, "hg38", as_rna = TRUE))
  m <- matrix(0L, nrow = length(seqs), ncol = W)
  for (i in seq_along(seqs)) {
    pos <- gregexpr(motif_regex, seqs[i], perl = TRUE)[[1]]
    pos <- pos[pos > 0]
    m[i, pos] <- 1L
  }
  m
}

sets <- list(SE = se_collapsed, background = non_event)
mats <- lapply(sets, function(gr) list(
  upstream   = flank_matrix(gr, "upstream"),
  downstream = flank_matrix(gr, "downstream")
))
sapply(mats, \(m) nrow(m$upstream))  # exons per set

# per-exon rolling mean over smooth_nt, then mean +/- s.e. across exons. As in
# slPlotFlankProfilesByNt(), both introns share one x axis: the upstream intron
# at x = 1..W (-W..-1 nt), then a gap holding the exon bar, then the
# downstream intron (+1..+W nt).
gap <- 60
profile_df <- function(m, side, set) {
  sm <- t(apply(m, 1, \(x) as.numeric(stats::filter(x, rep(1 / smooth_nt, smooth_nt), sides = 2))))
  pos <- if (side == "upstream") -W:-1 else 1:W
  tibble::tibble(
    set  = set,
    side = side,
    x    = if (side == "upstream") pos + W + 1 else pos + W + gap,
    mean = colMeans(sm, na.rm = TRUE),
    se   = apply(sm, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(nrow(sm))
  )
}

set_labels <- sprintf("%s (n = %d)", names(mats), sapply(mats, \(m) nrow(m$upstream)))
map_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(mats), function(s) dplyr::bind_rows(
  profile_df(mats[[s]]$upstream, "upstream", s),
  profile_df(mats[[s]]$downstream, "downstream", s)
))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(set = factor(set, levels = names(mats), labels = set_labels))

# x axis: nt from the exon every 100, the splice sites at the inner ends, and
# the exon bar in the middle (same labelling as .slFlankXAxis())
exon_x <- W + (gap + 1) / 2
bp <- seq(100, W, by = 100)
x_breaks <- c(rev(-bp) + W + 1, W, exon_x, W + gap + 1, bp + W + gap)
x_labels <- c(rev(-bp), "\n3'ss", "exon", "\n5'ss", paste0("+", bp))

# SE in its event_palette() colour, solid; background grey, dashed
map_cols <- setNames(c(sl_events[["se"]], "grey50"), set_labels)
map_lty  <- setNames(c("solid", "dashed"), set_labels)

ggplot(map_df, aes(x, mean, group = interaction(side, set))) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se, fill = set),
              alpha = 0.25, colour = NA, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = set, linetype = set), linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  # the exon as a grey bar in the gap, and a black x-axis line under each
  # intron, broken at the exon
  .slFlankExonBar(W, gap, exon_x) +
  .slFlankXLine(W, gap) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = map_cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = map_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = map_lty) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = x_breaks, labels = x_labels) +
  # from 0, with no padding below, so the x-axis line sits exactly on 0
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(title = "PTBP1 RNA map: YCUY motifs around SE exons",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d-nt rolling mean ± s.e.", smooth_nt),
       x = "Relative position in intronic sequence (nt)",
       y = "YCUY motif density per nt", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  .slFlankTheme() +
  theme(legend.key.width = grid::unit(1.2, "cm"))
```

Caveats: a 4-mer cannot start in the last 3 upstream positions without running
into the exon, so those columns are always 0; the overlapping count gives long
CU runs, such as the polypyrimidine tract, a lot of weight; and flanks of
introns shorter than `W` run into the neighbouring exon.

## Example SE gene: SMAP1

Two panels: isoform usage per sample, and the events `find_all_events()`
called in the gene. SMAP1 has two isoforms that differ by one 81-nt exon (plus
their 5' and 3' ends). The exon-including isoform has higher usage in KD, so
PTBP1 represses the exon. To plot another gene, add it to `example_genes`.

Usage is each transcript's share of the gene's counts in the unfiltered
matrix. Each DTU transcript (FDR < 0.1, the ones the events come from) gets its
own colour: shades of the up colour for higher usage in WT, shades of the down
colour for higher in KD. Every other transcript of the gene is pooled as
"other".

```{r example_genes, message=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
example_genes <- c(SMAP1 = "ENSG00000112305")

# KD first, then WT, numbered within condition in donor order
ord <- order(factor(raw_cond, levels = c("KD", "WT")), se_raw$donor, colnames(se_raw))
samp_lab <- character(ncol(se_raw))
samp_lab[ord] <- ave(raw_cond[ord], raw_cond[ord], FUN = \(x) paste0(x, "-", seq_along(x)))

# the package colour, then two lighter shades of it, for genes with more than
# one DTU transcript in a direction
shades <- \(col) grDevices::colorRampPalette(c(col, "white"))(5)[1:3]
pal_up   <- shades(sl_up)
pal_down <- shades(sl_down)

plot_example_gene <- function(gene, gene_id) {
  ex_events <- events[sub("\\..*", "", events$gene_id) == gene_id]
  ex_exons  <- sig_exons[sub("\\..*", "", sig_exons$gene_id) == gene_id]

  # the DTU transcripts, WT-up first, each ordered by effect size
  ex_res <- dtu_res |>
    dplyr::filter(tx_name %in% unique(ex_exons$tx_id)) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(estimates > 0), dplyr::desc(abs(estimates)))
  up_tx   <- ex_res$tx_name[ex_res$estimates > 0]
  down_tx <- ex_res$tx_name[ex_res$estimates < 0]

  # legend labels: the transcript id alone
  labs_tx <- setNames(ex_res$tx_name, ex_res$tx_name)

  gene_cnt <- raw_cnt[raw_gid == gene_id, , drop = FALSE]
  iso <- ifelse(rownames(gene_cnt) %in% names(labs_tx),
                labs_tx[rownames(gene_cnt)], "other")
  iso_levels <- c(labs_tx[up_tx], labs_tx[down_tx], "other")
  iso_cols <- setNames(c(pal_up[seq_along(up_tx)], pal_down[seq_along(down_tx)], sl_grey),
                       iso_levels)

  usage_df <- rowsum(gene_cnt, iso) |>
    sweep(2, colSums(gene_cnt), "/") |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("isoform") |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-isoform, names_to = "sample", values_to = "usage") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      sample  = factor(samp_lab[match(sample, colnames(se_raw))], levels = samp_lab[ord]),
      isoform = factor(isoform, levels = iso_levels),
      # "KD-3" -> condition "KD" (one shared label under its samples), "3"
      condition = factor(sub("-.*", "", sample), levels = c("KD", "WT")),
      sample_n  = factor(as.integer(sub(".*-", "", sample)))
    )

  p_usage <- ggplot(usage_df, aes(sample_n, usage, fill = isoform)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.85) +
    # one panel per condition, its name once below its sample numbers
    facet_grid(~ condition, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", switch = "x") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = iso_cols, drop = FALSE) +
    # zoom, not scale limits: a stack can sum to 1 + rounding error, and scale
    # limits would drop that top segment as out of range
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(title = sprintf("%s: isoform usage per sample", gene),
         x = NULL, y = "Share of gene expression", fill = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(strip.placement = "outside",
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

  # the events splicelogic called in this gene, on the transcripts they came
  # from
  p_events <- plot_transcripts(ex_events, ex_exons, rescale_introns = TRUE) +
    labs(title = sprintf("%s: events called by find_all_events()", gene))

  list(usage = p_usage, events = p_events)
}

example_plots <- Map(plot_example_gene, names(example_genes), example_genes)
for (p in example_plots) {
  print(p$events)
  print(p$usage)
}
```
